sources.citation: Z'graggen, Johannes A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Kolom not included (Rai Coast western languages only added 1975). General note that 'the marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet'.

sources.citation: Claassen, Oren R. & Kenneth A. McElhanon. 1970. Languages of the Finisterre Range. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 11, Pacific Linguistics A-23: 45-78.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sect. 6.1 (pp.63-66) gives phonology notes per family; for the Rai Coast Stock only syllable structure and 'In Suroi stress is contrastive, but only on a limited number of words' (p.66). Kolom is named as a comparison language (p.63) but nothing is said about Kolom stress.

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm. 2019. A fragment of Papua New Guinea philology. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia 37: 42-63 (+ appendix).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: identifies Miklouho-Maclay's 'Singor' numerals and 1877 comparative list as Kolom (Z'graggen 1980) and cites Kolom buai 'star'; philological identification only, no phonology, no stress

sources.citation: Gray, Rachel, Hannah Paris, Daryl Pfantz, Dan Richardson & Juliann Bullock. 2015. A Sociolinguistic Survey of the Yabong [ybo], Migum [klm], Nekgini [nkg], and Neko [nej]. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2015-005. Dallas: SIL International. 103 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); the open copy could not be downloaded when a reader tried
sources.note: Only modern first-hand Migum/Kolom data (wordlists from Lamtub and Singor); SIL-PNG survey wordlists are phonetic and often mark stress; any remark on stress here would be the only one in print. Open PDF but sil.org sits behind an automated-access block JS challenge and the Internet Archive holds only challenge-page captures.

sources.citation: Roberts, John R. 1997. Switch-reference in Papua New Guinea: a preliminary survey. In Andrew Pawley (ed.), Papers in Papuan Linguistics No. 3, 101-241. Pacific Linguistics A-87. Canberra: Australian National University. doi:10.15144/PL-A87.101
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: same 'no information available' sentence as for Arawum; nothing on stress or tone. (The paper also lists the Yaganon and Peka families -- i.e. Ganglau/Dumun and Urigina/Danaru -- only at family level among 'miscellaneous Madang language families' with no information, sec. 2.2.54 p. 118.)

(part 2 columns Baj, Singor, Telyat, Mitebog, Tiara, Rio, Erempi; 76 items); editorial notes by D. D. Tumarkin, language identifications by V. I. Belikov. (= Glottolog's Miklucho-Maclay 1951:170-183, re-edited from the MSS)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology content for Kolom: c. 76-item Singor wordlist (sky tain, sun kei, moon tambuü, water jan, sea jog, fire pavai, stone nange, man paran, woman panu, head patiu, nose sumbi, eye ambpatun, ear kunglo, tongue muni, pig bui, dog goun, yam niai, taro nalo..) and numerals 1-20 (daimo, lala, kei, bodei, kulane, kunopatun-dain, kunopatun-lala, 10 kulalala, 20 kabilala) printed in plain Latin letters WITHOUT stress marks; no remark on accent. sources.citation: Z'graggen, Johannes A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Rai Coast languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-30. Canberra: ANU. (language B7 Kolom)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent. Introduction sect. 7 (p.vii-ix) describes a 'semiphonemic' transcription and lists fluctuating sounds per language (Kolom: z ~ ʒ ~ dʒ); no stress is marked anywhere in the Kolom column and stress is never discussed.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, Johannes A. 1975. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41. Canberra: Australian National University. vi+154 pp., maps. (B7 Kolom: population 209, villages Lamtub(-Silaba) 129, Singor 80; index 'KOLOM B7 (Lamtug, Langtub, Singor)'; concordance of earlier sources to Z'graggen's language codes)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: no phonology content (the words stress/accent/tone do not occur in the volume); classification, census, village lists, maps and a concordance of earlier names/wordlists only. It adds one primary Kolom record not in our bibliography: Mager, John F. 1952, Gedaged-English Dictionary (Columbus, Ohio), whose comparative village wordlists include Singor = Kolom (wordlist only, print).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, Johannes A. 1975. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study 1, Pacific Linguistics C-38: 569-612.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent; classification only. p.581 identifies Dempwolff's 'Langtub (now spelled Lamtub)' wordlist as Kolom.

sources.citation: Dempwolff, Otto. 1905. Beiträge zur Kenntnis der Sprachen von Deutsch-Neuguinea. Mitteilungen des Seminars für Orientalische Sprachen VIII (Abt. 1): 182-254. [transcription conventions p.182; 'II. Papuasprachen, a) Langtub' wordlist pp.240-243]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No Kolom stress rule stated. p.182 gives his notation convention: stress ('Betonung') was often left unmarked when it fell on the penultimate syllable; in the Langtub list (pp.240-242) most words are unmarked but a fair number carry an acute on the FINAL syllable (muní 'Tanzfest' vs unmarked muni 'Zunge'/'Bruder', kŭtú 'Erdbeben', săngó 'Weg', tătărék 'Huhn', kanáo 'Möwe', naimbé 'Kakadu', malú, büdyiníl 'Bart', sumbí 'Nase', kŭnulá 'Ohr', kăsanán 'Mücke').
